common_name: Milk and Honey Astilbe (Cream-White Plumed Astilbe)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in consistently moist, organically rich soil in shade to dappled shade; Milk and Honey bears soft cream-white plumes and needs steady moisture through the growing season to avoid leaf scorch.

directions: Plant crowns so the top of the rhizome sits 1-2 inches below the soil surface in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in shade to dappled shade; Milk and Honey produces feathery, plume-shaped flower spikes in a soft cream-white with faint honey-gold undertones, a gentler, more muted color than the vivid pinks and reds common in many astilbe cultivars, standing above deep green, finely divided foliage in early to mid summer. The pale plumes glow softly in a shaded border and pair particularly well with dark-leaved companions such as bronze heucheras or purple-leaved coral bells. Astilbe does not tolerate drought and will brown and decline quickly without steady moisture, so mulch well and water regularly through the growing season, especially in a hot, humid Gulf South summer. Leave the dried plumes standing through fall and winter for ornamental interest, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring.
